newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan frees 38 detained Indian children.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan frees 38 detained Indian children.

text.p: Pakistan, in a goodwill gesture ahead of talks next week with arch-rival India, released 38 Indian children on Sunday held for about three years after being detained when Indian fishing boats were seized.
Social worker Abdul Sattar Edhi and his wife Bilqis said the young Indians had left for Karachi airport on their way home from a children's village where they had been staying.
Their release coincided with the Hindu festival of Holi.

The children, dressed in white clothes, were given garlands of flowers, clothes and $200 each before they were driven to Karachi in a bus without a police escort, said Edhi, who runs the private Karachi-based Edhi Welfare Trust organisation.
The top civil servants of the Indian and Pakistani foreign ministries are due to meet in New Delhi from March 28 to 31 to revive a dialogue that has been stalled since January 1994.
The children were among more than 100 people detained aboard Indian fishing boats caught in Pakistani waters in recent years.
Pakistan has said it is ready to release all the Indian boats and crew it holds if India frees Pakistani boats and crew seized in Indian territorial waters.
